title: Sprint lifeline — noon capture
body:
Noon capture — sprint lifeline (living note)
Owner: Asha P. — quick personal log for today, what to sync, blockers to escalate. Drafted during walk between meetings. Not a polished doc — treat as scratchpad; TODOs will be prioritized and placed into tickets later.

Top context (30s):
- Goal: ship hosted-api v1.4 launch subset (latency optimizations + streaming fix) with canary to 10% traffic by EOD Fri.
- Success criteria for canary: p50 latency < 85ms for 512 tokens, zero regression in hallucination eval vs baseline (eval-suite run: eva-hosted/launch-2026-03).
- Risk: backend KV cache eviction causing cold-start throughput drop at scale; observed in last bench run (bench-0326).

Immediate checklist (noon):
- [ ] Confirm canary traffic gate is wired: rollout policy points to runtime tag "v1.4-canary" (ACTION: ping infra on slack).
- [ ] Confirm nightly eval suite ran after midnight and no new quality regressions (ACTION: Lena to surface eval summary).
- [ ] Attach final smoke-test prompt set to PR description: small/edge/long prompt categories.
- [ ] Add cost target note for finance: target <= $0.85 / 1k tokens after batching optimizations.

PRD edit notes (things to fold into the PRD before finalizing):
- Clarify: default caching TTL should be 'adaptive' not fixed 30s; include mechanism to override per-organization. Add small diagram for prefix vs KV cache semantics.
- Add migration paragraph: when we flip runtime kernel, how do dedicated pools handle it? Add a short rollback list: revert runtime tag -> force drain -> reapply previous model variant.
- Call out observability: need per-route token-level cost and p99 latency heatmap (link to dashboard query).

Stakeholder follow-ups (who/what):
- Infra (Noah): need confirmation on draining semantics and whether we can drain a host without eviction across dedicated pools. (Message sent @ 10:12 — awaiting reply).
- SRE (Jules): ask for runbook update for cache-pressure alert (thresholds + runbook steps). If no reply by 15:00 escalate to on-call lead.
- Sales/AE (Maya): confirm we don't break existing large-customer routes during canary (they're on dedicated). Quick call scheduled 14:00.
- Legal/Compliance: remind that private deployments require special audit logging toggled on when model telemetry enabled. (Drop a note into legal queue).

Launch checklist (concise — to be expanded for shiproom):
- Pre-launch:
  - [ ] Merge PR #3124 with smoke tests attached.
  - [ ] Confirm canary config: rollout 0% -> 10% -> 50% over 2 hours.
  - [ ] Slack channel: #launch-hosted-v1.4 (create if missing).
  - [ ] Pager rotations aware for canary window (SRE/infra).
- Canary:
  - [ ] Run quick eval (small prompt set) every 30 minutes during first 2 hours.
  - [ ] Watch quality regression dashboard; if any metric falls below 95% baseline, pause rollout.
  - [ ] Check cost telemetry for batching effectiveness (observe per-request token count distribution).
- Post-canary:
  - [ ] Ensure auto-fallback policy is set to previous runtime variant on error spikes.
  - [ ] Schedule retrospective + perf analysis 48 hours after full roll.

Smoke test seeds (local to paste into CI):
- short_prompt: "Summarize this email in one sentence."
- long_prompt: (500+ tokens) — use deck lorem sim test for token overflow behavior.
- edge_prompt: JSON-structured tool-call simulation (validate function call routing).

Operational playbook snippets (for quick copy to runbook):
- Cache-pressure alert:
  - Trigger: host_cache_evictions_per_min > 50 over 5m AND p95 latency increase > 20%
  - First step: identify affected host group, limit incoming canary traffic to 0% for that group
  - Second step: ask infra to increase cache capacity (if cloud) or reduce batching size for immediate relief
  - Fallback: route to model-quantized variant with same accuracy profile if available

Quick notes from this morning's calls (raw):
- Product review: PMs asked for clearer messaging around "quantization quality tradeoffs" — add a small FAQ item under release notes.
- Dev sync: Kernel selection will be feature-flagged; need to confirm flags are present in Dedicated control plane.
- Solutions eng: wants sample Terraform snippet for private deployments to pin runtime tag — add to docs repo.

Blockers to escalate (if unresolved by 16:00):
- Infra confirmation on drain semantics (ticket PRJ-4823).
- Missing smoke test attachments on PR #3124 (N/A -> I uploaded initial set at 09:20 but want QA to confirm).

Decision log (quick, inline):
- Decided: we will not enable aggressive prefix cache eviction for canary customers to reduce noise during initial ramp. (Reason: avoid false positives on latency regressions).
- To revisit after canary: whether adaptive TTL should be per-tenant (data shows some tenants benefit).

Async requests to put in Slack/Email (short snippets to paste):
- To infra (Noah): "Can you confirm host drain semantics for dedicated pools when we tag runtime v1.4-canary? Need drain-without-evict or we'll see cold-start throughput drops. Reply by 15:00 please."
- To SRE (Jules): "Please add cache-pressure runbook steps to PRJ-4830 and call out p95 thresholds. If not back by 15:00 I'll escalate to on-call lead."

Small wins to note (for shiproom):
- Batch optimizer reduced median cost by ~6% in bench-0330 run.
- Streaming fix avoided duplicate EOT tokens in 98% of test cases.

End-of-day micro-plan (what I will do after meetings):
- 16:30: triage infra/SRE replies and convert outstanding items into tickets.
- 17:00: final PRD edits and add diagrams.
- 18:00: update launch checklist + ping sales/legal for FYI.

Random thought — future follow-up item (not for this ship):
- Evaluate an "observability-sim" harness that can replay production prefix distributions through candidate kernels to estimate end-to-end cost before rollout. Could save we-rolled-back costs.

-- scratchpad end --
(Will move prioritized todos into Jira and a cleaned-up launch brief for shiproom later today.)
